actions.note: Setu's own camera: V4L2 on Linux, Media Foundation on Windows, AVFoundation on macOS (Windows and macOS type-checked; their live runs are the VM and the Mac checklist).

actions.what: Use the voice as a second key
Unlock the lock screen when Setu sees the user
actions.note: Linux: when the lock screen is woken (key, mouse or opening the lid), Setu checks the face and asks logind to unlock the session. Windows: Setu's credential provider on the lock screen runs the face check and hands Windows the sealed password (type-checked, live run in the VM). macOS is not built.

actions.what: Sign in after a restart when Setu sees the user
actions.note: Linux: a PAM module asks the root-side service, which runs the camera and the face check itself and fills the sealed system password, with no name to pick at GDM. Windows: Setu's credential provider watches for any enrolled person from the sign-in screen and hands Windows the sealed password (type-checked, live run in the VM). macOS: out of reach before login with FileVault on.

actions.what: Fill an admin prompt from the vault
actions.note: Linux: sudo and polkit through the PAM module, face plus a nod. macOS: "type my password" types the vault password into the focused authorisation dialog after a face check. Windows: the secure-desktop helper exists, filling from the vault is not built.

actions.what: Save a password in the vault
Sign in to a website from the vault
actions.note: With a password for the site in the vault, the same words go to vault.signin: a face check, then the address and password are filled through CDP or BiDi, only on that site's own pages. With none saved, Setu opens the sign-in page.

actions.what: Choose between several accounts by voice
actions.note: With several accounts for a site, Setu asks which one and takes the answer by voice or click; "sign in to google with my work account" picks it in the request (vault.rs unit test, needs saved entries so it is not routed here).
